# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary task is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black/white circles impose turn/straight rules

#### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop
*Loop passes through cell centers*

##### 1.2.1 With Regional Constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through rooms once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop must go straight or turn consistently through all white circles in each bold-line area; avoids black circles
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" in a specified order

##### 1.2.2 With Directional/Wind Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction determined by arrows; wind from black cells restricts movement direction

##### 1.2.3 With Black Cell Constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through all black circles with the circle as the midpoint of a straight segment

---

### 2. REGION/AREA DIVISION GAMES
*The primary task is to partition the grid into defined regions*

#### 2.1 Division into Rectangles/Squares
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number indicating its cell count
- **Choco Banana** — Divide into regions; black regions must be rectangles/squares, white regions must not be

#### 2.2 Division into Polyominoes
- **Fillomino** — Divide into blocks; each block filled with a number equal to its size; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per bold-line region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells must connect
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of black squares) in each bold-line region (exactly two black squares per region)
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes; numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell

#### 2.3 Division into L-Shaped Blocks
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows point toward the bend; numbers indicate block size

#### 2.4 Division into Matched Pairs (Color-Symmetric)
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing equal white and gray areas of identical shape
- **Nuritwin** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two same-size shaded blocks; all shaded cells connect globally

---

### 3. CELL-SHADING/COLORING GAMES
*The primary task is to determine which cells to paint black (or shade)*

#### 3.1 With Connectivity and Adjacency Rules
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form a connected wall; white cell groups each contain exactly one number indicating group size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Rooms have black cell counts; black cells cannot touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total visible white cells (horizontally + vertically); black cells cannot touch; white cells connect
- **Usowan** — Numbers indicate adjacent black cells, but exactly one number per bold-line room is deliberately wrong; black cells cannot touch; white cells connect

#### 3.2 With Shape Constraints on Shaded Regions
- **Choco Banana** *(also in 2.1)* — Black regions must be rectangular; white regions must not be rectangular
- **Kurotto** — Circled numbers indicate the sum of connected black cell groups extending from them
- **Nurimisaki** — Circle cells are "promontories" (white, with exactly one white neighbor); numbers indicate straight-line white cell length; no 2×2 of either color

#### 3.3 With Structural/Gravity Rules
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per given counts; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells must fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

#### 3.4 With Tile/Region Uniformity
- **Tilepaint** — Entire bold-line tiles are either all shaded or all unshaded; diagonal-number cells indicate black cell counts in their row/column segment; solution depicts an object outline
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade entire rooms to create a maze from S to G; circle rooms are on the shortest path; triangle rooms are not; no 2×2 uniformity

---

### 4. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to place or fill numbers into cells*

#### 4.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box with no repeats

#### 4.2 Region-Based Number Sets
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold-line room contains 1 through N (room size); duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N; arrow-black cells indicate which neighbor holds the largest value; same numbers in adjacent rooms cannot touch

#### 4.3 Block-Size Encoding
- **Fillomino** *(also in 2.2)* — Numbers fill blocks whose size equals the number
- **Chained Block** — Black cell blocks must each contain one number or "?"; all blocks must form corner-touching chains; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

#### 4.4 Crossword-Style Number Fitting
- **Nansuke** — Fill white cells with digits from a given list of numbers placed horizontally or vertically

#### 4.5 Snake/Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch sides; directional visibility rules restrict placement relative to black cells

---

### 5. PATH / CONNECTION GAMES
*The primary task is to draw non-looping paths or connections between elements*

#### 5.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (1 or 2 per pair); all islands must be connected; bridges cannot cross

#### 5.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill all cells

#### 5.3 Movement / Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally or vertically into their home country (one circle per region); numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; arrow paths are straight and non-crossing; gray area numbers must equal the sum of entering circles

---

### 6. SYMBOL / MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to place specific symbols or marks into cells*

#### 6.1 Light/Visibility Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

#### 6.2 Directional Mark Filling
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; bold-line territories have counts of each mark; — cannot extend more than 2 cells vertically; | cannot extend more than 2 cells horizontally

#### 6.3 Triangle Placement
- **Shakashaka** — Place half-black triangles in cells so remaining white areas form only rectangles/squares; numbers indicate adjacent triangle count

#### 6.4 Square/Block Placement with Growth Rules
- **Evolomino** — Place squares in cells forming blocks; each block contains one arrow; each successive block along an arrow's path adds one square to the previous block's shape

---

### 7. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC GAMES
*Games combining two or more distinct primary mechanics*

#### 7.1 Shading + Loop
- **Yajilin** *(also in 1.2.3)* — Determine black cell positions AND draw a loop avoiding them

#### 7.2 Shading + Maze/Path
- **Nurimeizu** *(also in 3.4)* — Shade rooms to construct a valid maze with specific shortest-path properties

#### 7.3 Number Placement + Region Division
- **Makaro** *(also in 4.2)* — Fill numbers into pre-divided rooms with arrow-based ordering constraints

#### 7.4 Path Drawing + Pencil Structure
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight groups of cells) and draw lines from their tips; line length determined by numbers within the pencil body

#### 7.5 Loop + Regional Alternation
- **Moon-or-Sun** *(also in 1.2.1)* — Loop traversal combined with strict room-by-room symbol alternation

---

## Secondary Classification Cross-Reference

| Constraint Type | Games |
|---|---|
| **No 2×2 uniformity** | Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Yajilin |
| **Connectivity required (white/unshaded)** | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Usowan, Nurimisaki |
| **Single connected shaded region** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **Rooms/bold-line regions** | Heyawake, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Moon-or-Sun, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Nurimeizu, Norinori, LITS, Double Choco, Nuritwin, Usowan, Suraromu |
| **Arrow/directional clues** | Yajilin, Hebi, Makaro, Sashigane, Evolomino, Yosenabe, Nagareru |
| **Numbered circles/islands** | Hashiwokakero, Akari, Kurotto, Nurimisaki, Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Same-shape prohibition** | Chained Block, LITS |
| **Gravity/drop mechanic** | Sto-stone |
